answer: Give every identity one human face. The registry sends a random gesture sequence and a fresh nonce; the applicant performs the gestures on a video call and reads the nonce aloud. Three agents at random match the face against the stored embedding — a mirror check exposing any replayed recording; a hollow profile with no face behind it is rejected. The watchers take a summit vote; a second identity sharing that face is refused. Making 10,000 fakes would need 10,000 people at $40 each and a 15-minute session apiece: $400,000 and 2,500 human-hours. No face can be cloned, no session sped up.
